newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait's new oil minister to attend OPEC.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait's new oil minister to attend OPEC.

text.p: Kuwait's newly-appointed oil minister said on Wednesday he would attend OPEC's November ministerial meeting but declined to comment yet on the major exporter's next move.

"Until now I have not met with officials (at Kuwait's Oil Ministry) and I did not take the constitutional oath (of office)," Isa al-Mazeedi told Reuters by telephone when asked if he would seek a higher quota for the OPEC heavyweight.
Kuwait on Tuesday night formed a new 14-man cabinet, naming U.S.-educated Mazeedi, born 1942, as oil minister.

Kuwait has a current Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) quota of two million barrels per day (bpd) but it has often said it would seek a rise of 200,000 bpd if the 11-nation group increased the total ceiling. The group has a ceiling of 25.033 million bpd.
A Gulf source earlier told Reuters key OPEC states, including linchpin Saudi Arabia, had no plans to seek a higher ceiling when OPEC meets in Vienna on November 27.
Mazeedi, a member of Kuwait's minority Shi'ite branch of Islam, has a masters degree in business administration and a bachelors in industrial engineering.
He replaces Abdul-Mohsen al-Mudej who resigned in September to seek re-election in last week's parliamentary polls. He won a seat.
